card.name: The warning to keep out of reach of children
card.fires_on: The word keep (or 'out of', 'stored') starting a keep-away-from-children instruction, right after a sentence about accidental poisoning, overdose or choking hazards. Also a period ending a fatal accidental ingestion sentence.

modes.label: The instruction to keep out of reach
modes.description: The word Keep or KEEP opening the out-of-reach-of-children warning after an iron overdose sentence.
modes.example: WARNING: Accidental overdose of iron-containing products is a leading cause of fatal poisoning in children under 6.<< KEEP>> THIS PRODUCT OUT OF REACH OF CHILD

modes.label: Household safety advice
modes.description: Keep, stored or 'of' in home-safety lists about hazardous small objects and medicines kept away from children.
modes.example: To avoid accidental injuries or choking,<< keep>> penknives, nail files, scissors

modes.label: The accidental ingestion warning
modes.description: The full stop closing a sentence about fatal accidental ingestion by children.
modes.example: Accidental ingestion of tramadol hydrochloride and acetaminophen , especially by children, can result in a fatal overdose of tramadol<<.>> ( 5.2 ) Concom

card.writes: It pushes toward words about danger and hazard, and away from words about habit and familiarity.
card.plain: It responds to label text about child poisoning that says the product should be kept out of reach.
evidence: WARNING: Accidental overdose of iron-containing products is a leading cause of fatal poisoning in children under 6.<< KEEP>> THIS PRODUCT OUT OF REACH OF CHILD
To avoid accidental injuries or choking,<< keep>> penknives, nail files, scissors
and other choking or suffocation hazards are<< stored>> out of reach of children.

wording_before.name: Keep out of reach of children
wording_before.plain: It lights up where a label warns about child poisoning and tells you to keep the product out of reach.
